topicName: Logical Backups using mysqldump and mysqlpump
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Logical Backups using mysqldump and mysqlpump in MySQL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Logical backups are essential for database administration, allowing you to export database definitions and data into SQL statements that can be easily transferred, edited, or restored. In MySQL, the two primary tools for this purpose are mysqldump and mysqlpump."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding mysqldump"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"mysqldump is the traditional, widely-used utility for performing logical backups. It works by connecting to the MySQL server, querying the database to retrieve table structures and data, and generating a file containing SQL commands to recreate the database."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Basic mysqldump Usage"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"To back up a single database entirely, use the following command in your terminal:"},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"mysqldump -u root -p my_database > my_database_backup.sql"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To back up all databases on the MySQL server, use the --all-databases flag:"},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"mysqldump -u root -p --all-databases > all_databases_backup.sql"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding mysqlpump"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"mysqlpump is a newer utility introduced in MySQL 5.7 designed to address performance bottlenecks of mysqldump. The primary advantage of mysqlpump is its ability to perform parallel processing for databases and tables, significantly speeding up backup times on multi-core systems."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Basic mysqlpump Usage"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"The syntax of mysqlpump is similar to mysqldump. To back up a specific database with parallel threads, use the --default-parallelism option:"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"mysqlpump -u root -p --default-parallelism=4 my_database > my_database_pump.sql"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Differences and Advanced Options"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Parallel Processing: mysqldump operates in a single thread, whereas mysqlpump supports multi-threading per database and table."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"User Accounts: mysqlpump can dump user accounts and grants as SQL statements by default, using the --include-accounts option."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Compression: mysqlpump supports built-in LZ4 compression for the output SQL statements using the --compress-output=LZ4 option."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Restoring Backups"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Regardless of whether you used mysqldump or mysqlpump, the restoration process is identical because both output standard SQL script files. You can restore a database using the mysql client:"},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"mysql -u root -p my_database < my_database_backup.sql"},{"order":22,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Both mysqldump and mysqlpump are powerful tools for logical backups in MySQL. Use mysqldump for compatibility and smaller databases, and switch to mysqlpump when managing large databases that benefit from multi-threaded parallel execution."}]
